rationale: Block 4 completes the survey of all major organelles; this explorer reinforces the structure–function link for each compartment before the student moves to membrane composition.
Block 7 completes the transport hierarchy from passive to active to vesicular; ordering them tests understanding of the energy requirement at each level.
Block 10 completes the fractionation and marker-enzyme table; dragging each marker onto its organelle fraction tests whether the student can apply this mapping to a laboratory setting.
Block 11 completes the survey of membrane and organelle disorders; these blanks test recall of the key molecular defect, diagnostic threshold and structural component in each condition.
Block 4 completes the cofactor–coenzyme–vitamin connection; these blanks test recall of which B vitamin provides which coenzyme, a high-yield association for BI2.1.
Block 6 completes the seven IUBMB enzyme classes; dragging each class name into its example sentence tests whether the student can classify enzymes by the reaction they catalyse.
Block 10 completes Michaelis–Menten kinetics; these blanks test whether the student understands the key relationships between Km, Vmax, substrate concentration and reaction order.

Block 13 completes enzyme inhibition including organophosphate poisoning; ordering the steps of poisoning and rescue tests whether the student can apply irreversible inhibition to a clinical emergency.

Block 17 completes the organ-specific enzyme-interpretation patterns; these blanks test whether the student can recall the key ratios and thresholds that distinguish hepatocellular, cholestatic and pancreatic injury.
